canonical.title: Check if array is sorted and rotated

narrative.title: Integrity Check on a Circular Log Buffer
narrative.scenario: A metrics collector keeps its timestamps in a circular buffer, so the stored sequence may look shifted after a restart. Before serving queries, the collector must prove the readings would read as non-decreasing if the ring were unrolled at the right point. Determine whether the buffer was originally sorted and then rotated by some number of positions, including zero.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers representing the buffer contents.
narrative.outputFormat: true if nums can be obtained by rotating a non-decreasing array, otherwise false.

testCases.explanation: Unrolling the ring after 5 gives 1,2,3,4,5, which is non-decreasing, so the buffer is a rotation of a sorted sequence.
No rotation of a non-decreasing sequence drops once and then rises again in the middle, so the answer is false.

hintLevels: Level 1: Unrolling the ring is not necessary - ask how many times the sequence goes down as you walk it.
Level 2: Count every adjacent pair where the left value is greater than the right value, and remember that the last element sits next to the first.
Level 3: A drop in the middle can be the rotation point, but two drops can never be repaired, and equal neighbours are never a drop.
